summary.headline: Hindustan Zinc Q1 FY27 record EBITDA of INR8,074 crores (59% margin) and net profit of INR5,469 crores, with zinc COP at USD851/t.
summary.overview: Hindustan Zinc posted its highest-ever quarterly revenue (INR13,747 crores, up 77% YoY), EBITDA (INR8,074 crores, up 109% YoY) and net profit (INR5,469 crores, up 145% YoY) in Q1 FY27. Mine metal output of 268,000 t was the highest first quarter in five years, and refined metal rose 4% YoY to 260,000 t. Zinc cost of production excluding royalty fell to USD851/t, the lowest since the underground transition, helped by by-product realisation and better grades. The company sold 10 kt of lead concentrate (about 9 t silver and 6 kt lead metal) and ended with net cash of INR5,572 crores. Leadership is changing: Arun Misra hands over to Amarendu Prakash as CEO from 1 August 2026, and Amit Gupta is the new CFO.

segments.name: Zinc (mined and refined)
segments.commentary: Mined metal output of 268,000 t and refined output of 260,000 t, with zinc COP at USD851/t excluding royalty. Management guides to 1.1 million t for FY27 and expects Q4 at 280–290 kt.

segments.name: Silver
segments.commentary: Silver output of 149 t, with 10–15 t estimated locked in WIP; excluding concentrate sales, about 158 t was extracted. Silver contributed about 46% of profitability; the company needs about 175 t per quarter to reach its 680 t target.

segments.name: Lead and lead concentrate
segments.commentary: Sold 10 kt of inferior-grade concentrate stock from the RD mine ramp-up, realising INR315 crores. Company policy remains not to sell concentrate, and remaining old inventory will be used in smelters first.

segments.name: Sulphuric acid and fertiliser
segments.commentary: Sulphuric acid prices are reported up about 200% YoY. The phosphoric acid portion of the fertiliser plant at Chanderiya is due in Q2, and the full fertiliser plant is due in Q1 FY28 pending environmental clearance; about INR500 crores spent to date.

guidance_outlook: FY27 mined metal guidance of 1.1 million t reiterated; management sees no need to revise it and expects no further smelter shutdowns.
Zinc COP guided at USD975–1,000/t, with Q1 beating it through by-product realisation.
FY27 growth capex guided at USD500–600 million; INR800 crores spent in Q1.
Net cash position expected to be maintained at FY27 exit, based on volume and price assumptions.
Dividend policy unchanged: minimum 30% of profit plus 5% of reserves.
250 KTPA Debari integrated smelter and about 650 kt total metal capacity including mines: estimated INR24,000–25,000 crores, 36-month build, Board approval expected by Q3 FY27.
Tailings reprocessing plant construction started; about 30–35 kt zinc expected after about 24 months, with a 6–8 month ramp-up.
capex_capacity: Debari 250 KTPA integrated zinc smelter: mine development started to match mining capacity; capex estimate at a straight-line rate of about INR12,000 crores per 250 kt, pending tender outcome in about one month.
Tailings reprocessing plant: construction started and site mobilisation for infrastructure completed; 30–35 kt zinc output expected.
Hot acid leaching plant at Dariba and phosphoric acid/fertiliser plant at Chanderiya: on track for Q2 completion (phosphoric acid portion); full fertiliser plant by Q1 FY28.
Rampura Agucha and Chanderiya/Dariba debottlenecking, plus the 160,000 t pa roaster, supported output in Q1.
REE/Yttrium block in Gundlupet, Karnataka: exploration 2–3 years; production expected around FY2031–32.
demand_pricing: Zinc averaged USD3,466/t in Q1 with a high of USD3,625/t; lead averaged USD1,954/t.
Silver moderated to USD73/troy oz from the prior quarter's higher levels.
Hedge book: 48 kt zinc open at USD3,162/t and 34 t silver at USD63/oz; no hedging done in FY27 so far.
Coal mix: linkage coal share fell to 36% from 54% a year earlier and 64% in Q4; imported coal costs were higher, lifting power and fuel costs QoQ.
Revenue was supported by stronger dollar, higher by-product realisation and concentrate sales.

qa_highlights.question: Why did power and fuel costs rise QoQ despite lower metal output and higher RE share?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited lower linkage coal materialisation due to mine conditions, plus costlier imported coal, partly offset by higher RE power use.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company revise FY27 production guidance and is 1.1 Mt achievable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is confident in 1.1 Mt: 260 kt in Q1 implies about 1,040 kt on a straight-line basis, and Q4 typically reaches 280–290 kt. No revision is planned.

qa_highlights.question: What net cash position is expected at FY27 exit?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects to remain a net cash company at FY27 exit, based on its volume and price assumptions.

qa_highlights.question: Clarify the SEBI observations on related party transactions and the corrective steps taken.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said omnibus approvals have value limits; an alarm now triggers at 80% of the approved value, prompting Board and Audit Committee re-approval.

qa_highlights.question: What is the timeline and capex for the 600+ kt smelter project?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex for the 650 kt including mines is estimated at INR24,000–25,000 crores; tendering is ongoing, a 36-month build is expected after Board approval, and Board approval is targeted by Q3 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Silver guidance and what is needed per quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says silver grades should improve in Q2–Q4 with better PPM ore, with the strongest output in Q4; the 680 t target is seen as achievable.

qa_highlights.question: What is the fertiliser/phosphoric acid timeline and economics?
qa_highlights.answer: Only the phosphoric acid portion is due in Q2; the fertiliser plant is pending environmental clearance and is expected by Q1 FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Any update on government stake sale and dividend policy after the Vedanta demerger?
qa_highlights.answer: Government stake sale is for the government to comment on. Dividend policy is unchanged: minimum 30% of profit plus 5% of reserves, with INR11/share already paid.

qa_highlights.question: Breakdown of the USD50/t QoQ COP reduction and by-product effect?
qa_highlights.answer: COP is in line with the USD975–1,000/t guidance; the additional benefit comes from by-product realisation, which is credited through the COP, and no separate quantification was given.

qa_highlights.question: Is the royalty ratio to revenue at a multi-quarter low because of sulphuric acid?
qa_highlights.answer: Sulphuric acid carries no royalty. Mineral royalty is set as a percentage of the LME price, so it is not a fixed percentage of revenue.

risks_watch: Silver output must average about 175 t per quarter for the rest of FY27 to reach 680 t; Q1 was 149 t with 10–15 t in WIP.
Input cost pressure from energy prices and coal mix (linkage coal 36% vs 54% a year earlier) could erode the COP gain.
Hedge losses of INR200 crores in Q1 and an open 48 kt zinc position at USD3,162/t may weigh on realisations if prices rise.
Leadership transition: new CEO takes over on 1 August 2026, and a new CFO has been appointed.
Related-party transaction governance: SEBI observations and new omnibus-limit alarm controls.
Fertiliser plant delayed by pending environmental clearance; full plant now expected in Q1 FY28.
Government stake sale speculation; no update from management.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on operations and cash generation, with the record quarter presented as a base for FY27 guidance. Management was measured on growth project timelines and noncommittal on the government stake sale and fertiliser unit economics.
key_quotes: we reported highest ever EBITDA of INR8,074 crores, resulting into a record net profit of INR5,469 crores, making a new milestone for the company.
we achieved the lowest quarterly zinc cost of production, excluding royalty, since underground transition to USD851 per ton, reflecting a decline of 16% year-on-year.
We still don't sell concentrate. We still have the same policy that we don't sell concentrate.
So yes, now everything is back, and we will -- we won't have any further shutdown, and we will deliver on our commitment of 1.1 million tons.

growth.why: Company reiterated FY27 mined metal guidance of 1.1 Mt and growth capex of USD500-600m (INR800 crore spent in Q1), with Q1 revenue up 77% and EBITDA up 109% driven by by-product realisation, pricing and better grades rather than new capacity; new Debari smelter is only at board-approval stage, so forward capacity backing is partial.

mgmt.note: Arun Misra hands over to Amarendu Prakash as CEO from 1 August 2026, and Amit Gupta is the new CFO; no explicit growth plan from new management was stated in the brief.
